dedupe_keys.name: fncs framework for network co simulation pnnl

description: FNCS is a co-simulation framework that lets separate simulators, typically power system and communication network tools, exchange messages and advance time together, so that control algorithms can be developed across diverse simulator software and hardware. Pacific Northwest National Laboratory developed it under Battelle Memorial Institute, and version 2.0 simplifies and extends the original release. It is a C library built on the ZeroMQ messaging library and its CZMQ binding, installed from source on Linux following the README. Coverage is not geographic: it couples whatever models users plug in. Format and access: source code in a public repository. Licence: a Battelle BSD-style licence that allows use, modification and redistribution with the copyright notice; free. Caveats: the README documents only Linux builds, recent maintenance was not checked because the repository pages block scripts, and PNNL's later HELICS framework is its successor for most uses. It supports coupled power-communication simulations for cascading failure studies and digital twin prototypes. Related catalogue records are HELICS and the CoSim Toolbox for HELICS.
